ceiling_directive: Complete the finite mixed-support atlas by eliminating nuisance variables on every L/R/E/D, rank-two, support-face, and residual-forest chart, yielding explicit within- and cross-chart target-agreement tests or legal target-changing lifts.
improvement_directive: Replace the generic raw-fiber unequal-target existential test with explicit target elimination on every finite atlas chart and prove cross-component agreement. This must cover coincident endpoints, inactive rows, all support faces, and IV residual-forest branches.
critique: The note proves exact semialgebraic decidability of PN/PS constancy by sampling one feasible point and asking whether another feasible point has a different target, but this is a generic existential reduction rather than the advertised observable rank/support/cycle rigidity criterion. The structural atlas proves an exhaustive union of local factorization modes, yet it does not eliminate the target on mixed-support components or provide the promised agreement tests and formulas; that load-bearing step remains explicitly open in oeq:mixed-support-elimination. Consequently, the framing claim that singular and boundary fibers are classified overstates what the structural results deliver: they are generically decidable and structurally enumerated, not explicitly classified by the cycle atlas. The GEUVADIS contribution is only an audit protocol, with no recovered table, compatibility verdict, target set, or uncertainty output. The fixed-alphabet complexity bounds also rely on broad Basu–Pollack–Roy algorithmic assertions without precise numbered source statements, limiting reproducibility of the claimed quantitative bounds. [D0.5.G projected paper-score gate: paper_score_ceiling 5.3 < 7.4, so the graded tier 'subfield' is capped at 'incremental'. The score assesses the delivered research package without credit for unfinished work.]
